the mind wanders spontaneously and that it tends to wander to the self.
the wandering mind is often focused on self-relevant thoughts, which recruit the same brain regions as directed self-referent thinking, but with a different pattern of activation.
the default network is activated when the mind wanders, and that this activation involves the medial prefrontal and other brain regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive, affective, and neural mechanisms of mind-wandering and self-reference.
the neural basis of mind wandering, the role of self-referential processing, and its consequences for the experience of the self and for long-term goal-directed behavior.
the neural basis of the spontaneous self-referential processes of the mind.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mind-wandering is the process by which the mind spontaneously drifts away from the present moment and becomes absorbed in thoughts and images unrelated to the immediate environment.
mind-wandering and self-related thoughts are two sides of the same coin.
the default network plays an important role in self-referential thinking, which is the basis of the self.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the default network plays a central role in self-referential cognition, and the wandering mind is a natural product of this network.
mind wandering is a form of self-directed cognition, which is closely associated with our personal goals and identity.
the wandering mind is not a passive, aimless activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mind wandering and directed thought recruit similar neural networks, and that the wandering mind is not only a source of distraction but also an important component of the self.
self-referential thinking is a fundamental component of our mental life.
the mind is not a passive bystander, and it is not a blank slate either.
